author: Rezu
quote:
Grand Theft Auto 6 — 0/10: This Is NOT Grand Theft Auto

I genuinely don't know what happened to Grand Theft Auto, but this is not the GTA I grew up playing.

First off, why am I spending the beginning **** Theft Auto game repairing somebody's house? I barely even know who these characters are, and I'm already being forced to do tedious chores. It took me longer than most people to get through that section, and it was incredibly annoying. Then the game has me going grocery shopping. Seriously? I'm playing GTA to experience crime, chaos, freedom, and an entertaining story, not to play some everyday-life simulator.

And then there's the ridiculous number of restrictions. You can't even pick up prostitutes anymore. You can't run over protesters. But here's the most ridiculous part: you can't even steal the cars in your own neighborhood!

Let that sink in. The game is literally called GRAND THEFT AUTO, and apparently, committing grand theft auto is off-limits in certain areas. How does that make any sense? Stealing cars is one of the most fundamental mechanics of this entire franchise. If I see a car parked in my neighborhood, why can't I steal it? Why are there suddenly all these arbitrary restrictions in a game that's supposed to be about freedom and criminal chaos?

There are so many roadblocks that it feels like the game is constantly telling you what you're allowed and not allowed to do. GTA used to be about giving players the freedom to do outrageous things in a fictional world. That's literally part of what made the franchise famous.

What really bothered me was the inconsistency. Apparently, you can shoot inside a regular nightclub, but not inside a gay nightclub. Why? I'm not asking for special treatment either way. I'm asking why a game that built its reputation on unrestricted, controversial gameplay suddenly has different rules depending on the location. It makes the world feel artificially restricted.

Then came the mission that finally made me quit. The game forces you into a gay strip club, where you have to sit through a lengthy sequence watching nearly naked men dance. At one point, there's a dude wearing a tiny pink G-string with his massive bulge practically shoved right in your face. Seriously, why am I being forced to sit through this? The worst part is that I couldn't skip it. Whether I tried first-person or third-person, I still had to play through it.

I don't care what kind of club it is. I don't want to be forced to sit through an uncomfortable strip club sequence that has nothing to do with why I bought the game, especially when there's no option to skip it.

What frustrates me most is that GTA used to be about player choice. You could explore, cause chaos, do ridiculous things, and enjoy a world that didn't constantly hold your hand or restrict your actions. Now it feels like I'm being forced through boring chores, selective restrictions, and uncomfortable missions instead of actually having fun.

I didn't buy Grand Theft Auto to repair houses, shop for groceries, or sit through unskippable strip club sequences. And I certainly didn't buy a game called Grand Theft Auto just to be told which cars I'm allowed to steal.

I bought it to play Grand Theft Auto.

Final score: 0/10.

I gave it a chance, but that strip club mission was the final straw. I stopped playing, and I have absolutely no desire to continue. For me, this game completely misses what made GTA special in the first place.
